label: Observed
subject: frozen dossier policy successor comparison
terminal_leaf_definition: JSON scalar values plus empty containers; array indices remain separate RFC6901 path components
methods: independent paired typed traversal and key/array-length assertions

changes.old: the shallow by-commit fetch from the target's upstream that the observation consent describes, for a repository whose visibility is public (sourceVisibility) only; for a private repository Syzygy fetches nothing, reads only Git objects already present in a clone the operator holds, and holds, reads, requests and uses no credential for the repository's host
changes.new: no network acquisition in the declared local-clone entry; private sources use no repository-host credential

changes.old: the registered provider route through the single egress check
changes.new: classified and screened content only to the declared provider under SEC-2; no secrets

changes.old: every other rule in this policy applies to this scope unchanged: detectors, matchAction and redactionClasses (except that secretRedaction retains a body of an admitted snapshot as redacted-span where its rule says so, and for such a body reads the detector condition of classificationSuccess as no detector matching its retained text), unclassifiableExclusion, activeContentClassification (except that, for a body activeContent.codeContentExemption or activeContent.projectDocumentationExemption exempts, its active-content forms are not scanned for and malformedContextAction does not apply; its renderRule binds every body) and the strict-UTF-8 and NUL rules. 'Every other rule' means the policy's rules outside any named scope object; the rules inside the base scope object, and inside any sibling scope object another act adds, do not govern this scope, and the other way round: the routes, boundaries, rawBodyHandling and rules written inside this object govern only the repositories in observedRepositories and never the base scope or a sibling scope. The base classificationOrder and classificationSuccess name the signed PWB grammar; under this scope they read: membership in the admitted snapshot replaces membership in a PWB phase, and the content-classification rules above replace the PWB closed extraction class, so a blob with no class under those rules has an unknown extraction class and is excluded whole (step 6), while a code-content body needs no extractor and is admitted as whole-blob spans. No approved requirement names this reading, so it is this policy's own and binds only through the act that approves it

The dossier declared-source specification names this reading; adoption follows VIS-4 and changes no other inherited rule

changes.old: exactly the repository ids named by an effective observation consent record, of a public or a private repository (sourceVisibility), whose subject is (project:syzygy, repository:<id>); the policy admits no repository: contentClassification's ownerPlacements name a repository only to place paths at commits its observation consent already admits, so admitting or withdrawing a target never edits the policy, and a placement whose repository or commit no effective consent names places nothing
changes.new: the repository identity and full pinned commit declared in a dossier run; public and private sources are admitted without observation, registry, policy or provider-statement acts; owner placements apply only to the exact declared repository and commit they name

changes.old: a consent record that does not list project-documentation does not permit its egress, and no consent granted before the class existed is read as covering it (RFC5-14 as amended); this policy confers no consent
changes.new: A declared provider is required for agent-bound content. The committed policy classifies project-documentation without a separate class or consent act; an undefined or unreadable class remains excluded. No provider declaration overrides screening

changes.old: the project-documentation rule classifies a blob only while the in-force RFC-0005 vocabulary lists project-documentation; a consumer that cannot confirm that treats every blob the rule names as indeterminate, and the rest of this scope is unchanged
changes.new: the committed classification rule defines project-documentation; a malformed or unrecognized rule refuses rather than guessing its class

changes.old: admit arbitrary repositories, public or private (sourceVisibility), to the Polaris generator: read their Git snapshot objects, screen them under this policy and classify them into RFC5-14 classes; a target repository's own text is data to screen, never policy (RFC3-30)
changes.new: classify and screen declared local dossier sources under SEC-5; target text is data, never policy

changes.old: storage is permitted only inside a run directory under project:syzygy's state directory, outside git; rendering only in a generated editorial draft; external egress only for content this scope classifies and only under a separate egress consent for the pair; for a repository whose visibility is private, an egress consent covers its content, target-metadata included, only when its record names that pair and states that the repository is private, so a public-target egress consent, or one that does not state it, never covers it
changes.new: storage is permitted only inside the local run directory outside git; no raw body logging or machine response; rendering is an editorial draft only. Content delivered to a provider must be classified and screened and the provider declared under SEC-2. Secrets never leave. Excluded or withheld private object identifiers and sizes are never rendered or sent and remain only in permitted local check records and review packets

changes.old: the commit object ids listed by the observation consent; a tag name is a label only
changes.new: the full commit pinned in the dossier run and the tree and blob objects reachable from its root tree; tag and branch names are locator provenance only

changes.old: the limits declared by the registered source-acquisition entry for the fetch; a limit failure excludes the whole artifact as unclassifiable-excluded
changes.new: the existing bounded dossier object reader and declared finite run limits; removing a registry act changes no configured bound or breach result

changes.old: [Observed] REQ-polaris-generation-033 says that neither the content classes a per-project statement names nor the observing project's classification and screening policies bind the operator-agent mode's agent sessions' own reads or sends: the agent reads the clone without restriction, and content those policies would exclude, secrets included, may reach the agent's provider. This policy binds what Syzygy reads, stores, renders and sends; it cannot keep a private repository's content, or a secret in it, from the agent's provider. Whether a private subject that REQ-polaris-generation-033 calls non-governed needs a per-project statement before a brief is issued is the specification's to decide, not this policy's
changes.new: SEC-2 and SEC-5 bind agents as well as Syzygy: only the declared provider may receive content, and secrets never leave. Briefs require agents to preserve screening and exclusion rules in their own reads and sends. Syzygy screens the content it reads, stores, renders and delivers; it cannot observe or attest an agent tool own transmissions or compliance, which are never presented as Observed

changes.old: [Inferred] a launch consent record carries the repository's declared identity and normalised URL and is committed into the observing project's own governance repository, on a dedicated reference Syzygy never pushes (REQ-polaris-generation-046); for a private repository that makes its name, host path and commit ids tracked objects of Syzygy's repository, one push by the operator from its remote. This scope does not govern those records and cannot change it; the specification does
changes.new: No launch consent record, dedicated recording reference or governance write is made for source admission. Repository identity, normalized locator, visibility and pinned revision are stored as Inferred run declarations in the local state directory, within the agent sessions write reach; they are not authorization records

changes.old: [Inferred] a run on a repository whose record does not state public is no longer refused for want of a policy admitting it, and runs under the stricter rules above: its project-documentation bodies with a detector match are withheld whole where a public repository's keep every line outside the withheld ones, so its dossier can withhold more files and render more Unknown; Syzygy reads it only from a clone the operator already holds; and no request Syzygy makes carries its content until an egress consent stating it private is in force. The reason for the redaction rule: a retained redacted-span body shows every line but the withheld ones, and the whole body's content digest and Git object id stay recorded (RFC5-17), so a guess at a short withheld line can be confirmed against them offline; for a public repository the body is published already and this adds nothing, for a private one it would. Whole exclusion does not close the guess either: the content digest, and the Git object id, which is itself a digest of the whole body, are a confirmation oracle wherever a guesser knows the rest of the body (a private fork of a public upstream whose file differs by one secret line, a template, earlier public history), and the size narrows the secret's length. For a public repository the object id and size are code-structure, rendered on the dossier's pages and carried by an egress consent that lists code-structure. For a private repository this version withholds them for every blob excluded or withheld on any ground, a denied path, an indeterminate blob and a detector match among them: they are kept, if at all, only in the run directory's check records and its local review packets, and are never rendered or sent. What is left: the run directory itself and the operator's clone, which holds every object id, so whoever can read either can still confirm a guess; the pinned commit id, rendered on every discovery row and recorded in the launch record, which is a digest of the commit header and the root tree and so of every object id in it, the withheld blob's included, a narrower confirmation oracle open only to a guesser who also knows the commit header (its author, dates, message and parent) and the rest of the tree, and one this scope cannot withhold; and a secret no detector matches in a body this scope admits, which is admitted and rendered under either visibility (SEC-5's general residual, unchanged here). A pair that a private fork's record joins, or that holds a record stating nothing or unreadable, becomes private, so its public upstream's runs get the stricter rules too, its public-target egress consent among them. Launch consent records lie within the agent sessions' write reach, so one malformed or unreadable file written there refuses every read under this scope, every public repository's included, until it is read or revoked: a cost to availability, never to exposure
changes.new: A private or undeclared-visibility local source is admitted with stricter whole-body exclusion and private withheld metadata protection; it may therefore yield more Unknown items. No provider transmission is observed merely because a provider is declared. The reason for the redaction rule: a retained redacted-span body shows every line but the withheld ones, and the whole body's content digest and Git object id stay recorded (RFC5-17), so a guess at a short withheld line can be confirmed against them offline; for a public repository the body is published already and this adds nothing, for a private one it would. Whole exclusion does not close the guess either: the content digest, and the Git object id, which is itself a digest of the whole body, are a confirmation oracle wherever a guesser knows the rest of the body (a private fork of a public upstream whose file differs by one secret line, a template, earlier public history), and the size narrows the secret's length. For a public repository the object id and size are code-structure, rendered on the dossier's pages and eligible as classified content for the declared provider. For a private repository this version withholds them for every blob excluded or withheld on any ground, a denied path, an indeterminate blob and a detector match among them: they are kept, if at all, only in the run directory's check records and its local review packets, and are never rendered or sent. What is left: the run directory itself and the operator's clone, which holds every object id, so whoever can read either can still confirm a guess; the pinned commit id, rendered on every discovery row and recorded in the run record, which is a digest of the commit header and the root tree and so of every object id in it, the withheld blob's included, a narrower confirmation oracle open only to a guesser who also knows the commit header (its author, dates, message and parent) and the rest of the tree, and one this scope cannot withhold; and a secret no detector matches in a body this scope admits, which is admitted and rendered under either visibility (SEC-5's general residual, unchanged here).

changes.old: a private repository is admitted under the same observation consent as a public one, and every rule of this scope applies to it as to a public one, except at four sites, each stricter: accessBoundary.networkEgressRoutes (Syzygy fetches nothing and uses no credential for the repository's host); secretRedaction.appliesTo (no body is retained as redacted-span: a detector match excludes the whole body in every class); rawBodyHandling.rule (an egress consent covers the repository's content only when its record names the pair and states that the repository is private); and contentClassification's code-structure rule, which indeterminate follows (the object id and size of a blob excluded or withheld on any ground are not code-structure, are never rendered and never leave the run directory). No rule of this scope is relaxed for a private repository. No rule for a public repository changes, except in two ways, both fail closed: a public repository reads private while any other effective record of its pair states private, states nothing or cannot be read, and a file that could be a record of any pair (its kind, effectiveness or pair unread) refuses every read under this scope, public repositories included
changes.new: a private repository is admitted as a declared local source under the same rules as a public one, except at three stricter sites: accessBoundary.networkEgressRoutes (no repository fetch and no host credential); secretRedaction.appliesTo (no redacted-span body: any detector match excludes the whole body in every class); and contentClassification code-structure and indeterminate rules (an excluded or withheld blob object id and size are never rendered or sent and remain only in permitted local check records and review packets). No detector, exclusion or private metadata rule is relaxed. A declared provider is required for content delivery under SEC-2; no separate egress consent is required

changes.old: visibility is decided for each commit Syzygy reads, from the effective observation consent record that admits that commit (the record of that pair naming that revision), and it is public only when that record states public through its carrier and every other effective observation consent record of the same pair states public through its carrier too; in every other case, including a record that states private, states nothing, or cannot be read, the repository is private for every rule of this scope at every commit. A fork or mirror that a record places in an upstream's pair is part of that pair, so its record stating private makes the whole pair private. The carriers, and the only ones: for a launch consent record, the operator's declaration whether the repository is public that REQ-polaris-generation-046 requires the record to carry, which states public only when it is the affirmative answer, read by the generic launch form as one of exactly two values; for a record made by the owner act recorded at .syzygy/governance/decisions/PUBLIC-REPO-ADMISSION-REDIS-OBSERVATION-ACT.md or at .syzygy/governance/decisions/PUBLIC-REPO-ADMISSION-REQUESTS-OBSERVATION-ACT.md, and by no other act, that act's form itself, which states public; a further act states public by its form only when a later version of this policy names it, never because a code list of act forms grows. No other text of a record, its title or prose included, is a carrier. Every file at a location where observation consent records are read counts as a possible one: for launch consent records, every file that a recording commit on the dedicated reference added at the launch records' location (a recording commit adds new files only), a drawer or provider statement included, and no file the reference holds that no recording commit added; for the act forms, each act file named above. Any such file not shown to be revoked or superseded whose kind cannot be read, or that reads as an observation consent record whose effectiveness or pair cannot be read, including one that cannot be read at all, could be a record of any pair, so while one exists every read under this scope is refused, with that file named, until it is read or revoked; this scope does not instead ignore it, guess its kind or pair or turn every pair private. The statement is the operator's or the owner's declaration and is labelled Inferred wherever it is shown: Syzygy makes no network request and uses no credential to learn or verify it. admitted lists the visibilities this scope admits; a repository of a visibility it does not list is not in observedRepositories
changes.new: visibility is declared for the exact repository and pinned commit in the dossier run, with its source attributed and labelled Inferred. Only an explicit public declaration gets public treatment. Private, missing or ambiguous declarations get private treatment; malformed declarations refuse. Syzygy makes no network request and uses no credential to verify visibility, and never infers it from a host, scheme, user name or credential use. No consent or act record supplies or overrides this declaration
